messages:
maria_finance: Heads up — noticed a new line on the March invoice: 'Commitment reallocation fee' for $12,146. Appears under us-west1 but the allocation shows ap-southeast1 projects. Invoice PDF: https://billing.redwood.internal/invoices/2026-03 (paywalled). :eyes:

aj_infra: Looking into billing export now. Quick BigQuery to surface SKU and commitment IDs:
```sql
SELECT sku_description, commitment_id, region, SUM(cost) AS cost
FROM `redwood-billing.gcp_export.billing_export_v2`
WHERE invoice_month = '2026-03'
  AND sku_description LIKE '%commit%realloc%'
GROUP BY sku_description, commitment_id, region
ORDER BY cost DESC;
```

drew_billingbot: Automated alert: new billing SKU detected: COMMITMENT_REALLOC. Created ticket #BILL-402 and notified finance.

sylvia_ops: We did a manual capacity rebalance for Dedicated pools on Feb 27 (moved ~40 GPUs from ap-southeast1 -> us-west1 to handle a temporary burst). Did we request reallocation that would trigger a charge? :thinking_face:

aj_infra: We triggered a cold-pool reclamation script but that should not touch committed reservations. I don't see any manual 'convert' or 'reassign' calls in infra logs. Querying cloud console for commitment IDs now.

aj_infra: Quick result snippet — billing export shows two entries with the same commitment_id (cid-7f4a) that have costs in both ap-southeast1 and us-west1, and a positive cost for COMMITMENT_REALLOC of $12,146 tagged to project-prod-reserved. Could be a cross-region reallocation fee from the provider.

maria_finance: Is this an AWS RI conversion fee, or a GCP committed use reallocation charge? We normally avoid cross-region moves. If it's the provider's penalty, we should request a refund. @ops-support can you open a support case with the provider and attach the invoice line?

ops-support: Opening case with GCP now. Case created: 0123456789 — "Unexpected commitment reallocation charge affecting reserved GPU pool". Asking for breakdown by commitment_id and timestamp. ETA for first response 24-48h. :white_check_mark:

sylvia_ops: FYI we did one migration that touched dedicated pool metadata via the orchestration engine to free capacity, but I assumed the reserved commitments would be untouched. Will dig into orchestration audit logs for Feb 26-28.

aj_infra: Found orchestration log snippet that shows a housekeeping job calling the pool allocator with region hints. Not an explicit reassign, but there is a codepath that will 'convert' a soft-reservation when capacity is tight. Posting excerpt:
```
2026-02-27T23:48:12Z pool-allocator INFO convert-reservation cid=cid-7f4a from=ap-southeast1 to=us-west1 reason=burst-handling
```

sylvia_ops: Ugh. That looks like our bug — the allocator shouldn't convert committed reservations without an explicit approval. :facepalm:

maria_finance: Okay, action items: (1) ops to confirm whether conversion API call triggered a provider-side fee (ops-support already on it), (2) infra to flag allocator codepath as emergency stop and roll back conversion behavior, (3) finance to request provisional credit from provider. I'll cc legal if they push back.

aj_infra: Putting emergency stop now — disabling the convert-reservation path in the allocator and creating a canary to ensure we don't accidentally run conversion on other commitments. PR raised: https://github.com/redwood/allocator/pull/214 :thumbsup:

ops-support: GCP case update: initial reply says these are "commitment transfer fees" applied when a commitment is changed across regions. They're asking for the exact timestamps and API request IDs to evaluate refund. Requested we provide allocation audit logs.

maria_finance: I'll prepare a chargeback analysis and a refund request template. Can someone paste the audit lines and API request IDs here? We need them in the support case.

aj_infra: Pasting the audit IDs we have so far: [req-789a, req-78fb, req-78ff]. Also attaching the allocator audit export to the support case.

sylvia_ops: I've searched the orchestration logs and found the three convert-reservation calls. They match req-789a/78fb/78ff. Adding a short incident note to postmortems/ops.

maria_finance: Thanks. Finance will draft the refund request and check the commitment record to ensure we don't get charged again. For the immediate cycle, please block any automated reassignments of committed resources.

aj_infra: Confirmed — emergency stop in place and new unit tests added. I'll follow up in #eng-runtime once the allocator patch is deployed to prod.

maria_finance: Closing loop for now — assigned to @aj_infra and @sylvia_ops to drive refund + root cause. Finance will log the $12,146 as a one-off expense pending resolution. Marking as actioned in our internal tracker. :white_check_mark:
